# FetchCore Repository Knowledge, Retrieval, and Serving Boundaries

## Canonical source of truth

Repository sources pass through materialization, safe scanning, corpus/document policy, and `RepositoryIndexer` extraction. The canonical unit is `KnowledgeDocument`, carrying typed `KnowledgeEvidence`, `KnowledgeProvenance`, repository, revision, path, line span, and checksum. KnowledgePacks and source-derived relationships enrich this knowledge but do not make a source authoritative. Solr, OpenSearch, Qdrant, and other indexes are rebuildable projections, not canonical storage; changing or rebuilding a vendor schema must not redefine source evidence. Sources: `docs/architecture/repository-knowledge.md`, `docs/architecture/projection.md`.

## Intent, scope, and execution policy

`SearchIntent` declares retrieval meaning independently of corpus authorization and execution policy. Its v2 fields include the unchanged `canonical_query`, required `anchors`, an optional required `SearchExpression` tree (`Term`, `Anchor`, `AllOf`, `AnyOf`), caller-attributed `expansions`, weak `hints`, typed `signals`, and v1-compatible exact/semantic terms. FetchCore does not infer anchors, boolean structure, or synonyms from natural language. Expansions increase recall without relaxing required structure; hints remain preferences.

`SearchScope` defines where and how broadly retrieval may operate: workspace, repository, revision, repository paths, knowledge types, maximum results, mode, settings, and optional retrieval configuration. `SearchRequirement` is a bounded allocation hint, not a satisfaction decision. `RetrievalConfig` selects acquisition behavior such as lexical, dense, or hybrid mode. Sources: `docs/concepts/search-intent.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/contracts.py`, `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`.

## Unsupported required semantics

The policy is fail-closed rejection. There is no configurable flattening fallback. Before scanning, backend I/O, or embedding, adapters validate whether every participating channel can preserve required canonical text, anchors, and expressions. Unsupported required constructs raise `KnowledgeSearchError` with category `unsupported_semantics` and translation policy `reject`. Optional expansions, hints, and signals may remain unconsumed and be reported as `partially_unsupported` without rejecting retrieval. Hybrid currently rejects anchors or boolean groups because fusion cannot guarantee those constraints and there is no post-fusion constraint engine. Unsupported retrieval modes likewise raise a typed `unsupported_capability` error; FetchCore does not silently substitute lexical for dense or vice versa. Sources: `docs/concepts/search-intent.md`, `docs/reference/capabilities.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/config.py`.

## Current retrieval channels and adapters

Current acquisition paths are local lexical scanning, backend lexical/BM25, dense vector retrieval, and backend hybrid retrieval where advertised capabilities permit them. Built-in retrieval adapters are `local-semantic` (local lexical scanning), `solr` (lexical/dense/hybrid plus current operational index synchronization), `opensearch` (lexical/dense/hybrid), and `qdrant-vector` (dense and hybrid vector/sparse acquisition; standalone lexical is not implied). `ollama` is a separate embedding provider, not a retrieval backend. The backend-neutral `KnowledgeSearchBackend.search(intent, scope, requirements)` port returns `KnowledgeSearchResponse` containing provenance-preserving `SearchResult` evidence. Graph traversal, a general identifier-first targeted router, and federated multi-repository fusion are not current mandatory retrieval paths. Sources: `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`, `docs/reference/capabilities.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/contracts.py`.

## Hybrid baseline

Hybrid independently acquires lexical or sparse candidates and dense candidates, then fuses them with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), the configured baseline. `RetrievalConfig` currently accepts only `rrf` as its hybrid strategy. Optional reranking occurs after acquisition and is bounded by an explicit candidate window; reranking is not a backend capability gate. Scores and fusion ranks are retrieval observations, not correctness, satisfaction, or authority. Sources: `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/config.py`.

## MCP serving boundary

The serving path is `MCP stdio → application runtime bootstrap → RetrievalApplicationService → KnowledgeSearchBackend`. MCP is a transport adapter: it exposes `search` and bounded `get_source`, but does not call Solr, OpenSearch, Qdrant, or local backend APIs directly and does not own retrieval translation or agent lifecycle. The application service creates repository-scoped requests, bounds result/source reads, and rejects unauthorized paths through a `RepositoryBinding`. P0 binds one authorized repository per server process; federated MCP search, HTTP/auth/ACL serving, `find_symbol`, and graph-backed `get_related` are deferred. Sources: `docs/architecture/serving.md`, `docs/guides/mcp.md`.

page.title: FetchCore Repository Knowledge, Retrieval, and Serving Boundaries
page.body:
# FetchCore Repository Knowledge, Retrieval, and Serving Boundaries

## Canonical source of truth

Repository sources pass through materialization, safe scanning, corpus/document policy, and `RepositoryIndexer` extraction. The canonical unit is `KnowledgeDocument`, carrying typed `KnowledgeEvidence`, `KnowledgeProvenance`, repository, revision, path, line span, and checksum. KnowledgePacks and source-derived relationships enrich this knowledge but do not make a source authoritative. Solr, OpenSearch, Qdrant, and other indexes are rebuildable projections, not canonical storage; changing or rebuilding a vendor schema must not redefine source evidence. Sources: `docs/architecture/repository-knowledge.md`, `docs/architecture/projection.md`.

## Intent, scope, and execution policy

`SearchIntent` declares retrieval meaning independently of corpus authorization and execution policy. Its v2 fields include the unchanged `canonical_query`, required `anchors`, an optional required `SearchExpression` tree (`Term`, `Anchor`, `AllOf`, `AnyOf`), caller-attributed `expansions`, weak `hints`, typed `signals`, and v1-compatible exact/semantic terms. FetchCore does not infer anchors, boolean structure, or synonyms from natural language. Expansions increase recall without relaxing required structure; hints remain preferences.

`SearchScope` defines where and how broadly retrieval may operate: workspace, repository, revision, repository paths, knowledge types, maximum results, mode, settings, and optional retrieval configuration. `SearchRequirement` is a bounded allocation hint, not a satisfaction decision. `RetrievalConfig` selects acquisition behavior such as lexical, dense, or hybrid mode. Sources: `docs/concepts/search-intent.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/contracts.py`, `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`.

## Unsupported required semantics

The policy is fail-closed rejection. There is no configurable flattening fallback. Before scanning, backend I/O, or embedding, adapters validate whether every participating channel can preserve required canonical text, anchors, and expressions. Unsupported required constructs raise `KnowledgeSearchError` with category `unsupported_semantics` and translation policy `reject`. Optional expansions, hints, and signals may remain unconsumed and be reported as `partially_unsupported` without rejecting retrieval. Hybrid currently rejects anchors or boolean groups because fusion cannot guarantee those constraints and there is no post-fusion constraint engine. Unsupported retrieval modes likewise raise a typed `unsupported_capability` error; FetchCore does not silently substitute lexical for dense or vice versa. Sources: `docs/concepts/search-intent.md`, `docs/reference/capabilities.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/config.py`.

## Current retrieval channels and adapters

Current acquisition paths are local lexical scanning, backend lexical/BM25, dense vector retrieval, and backend hybrid retrieval where advertised capabilities permit them. Built-in retrieval adapters are `local-semantic` (local lexical scanning), `solr` (lexical/dense/hybrid plus current operational index synchronization), `opensearch` (lexical/dense/hybrid), and `qdrant-vector` (dense and hybrid vector/sparse acquisition; standalone lexical is not implied). `ollama` is a separate embedding provider, not a retrieval backend. The backend-neutral `KnowledgeSearchBackend.search(intent, scope, requirements)` port returns `KnowledgeSearchResponse` containing provenance-preserving `SearchResult` evidence. Graph traversal, a general identifier-first targeted router, and federated multi-repository fusion are not current mandatory retrieval paths. Sources: `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`, `docs/reference/capabilities.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/contracts.py`.

## Hybrid baseline

Hybrid independently acquires lexical or sparse candidates and dense candidates, then fuses them with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF), the configured baseline. `RetrievalConfig` currently accepts only `rrf` as its hybrid strategy. Optional reranking occurs after acquisition and is bounded by an explicit candidate window; reranking is not a backend capability gate. Scores and fusion ranks are retrieval observations, not correctness, satisfaction, or authority. Sources: `docs/architecture/retrieval.md`, `src/fetchcore/retrieval/config.py`.

## MCP serving boundary

The serving path is `MCP stdio → application runtime bootstrap → RetrievalApplicationService → KnowledgeSearchBackend`. MCP is a transport adapter: it exposes `search` and bounded `get_source`, but does not call Solr, OpenSearch, Qdrant, or local backend APIs directly and does not own retrieval translation or agent lifecycle. The application service creates repository-scoped requests, bounds result/source reads, and rejects unauthorized paths through a `RepositoryBinding`. P0 binds one authorized repository per server process; federated MCP search, HTTP/auth/ACL serving, `find_symbol`, and graph-backed `get_related` are deferred. Sources: `docs/architecture/serving.md`, `docs/guides/mcp.md`.
